strengths: Broad collection of black-box optimization algorithms: The manuscript details an ambitious scope covering over 72 variants across 13 families of population-based methods within a unified Python interface.
Good design emphasis on modularity and standard ecosystem compatibility (NumPy, SciPy, Numba) targeting high-dimensional zeroth-order optimization problems.
weaknesses: Lack of technical or empirical contribution: The submission reads as an open-source software announcement (similar to a JMLR MLOSS short paper) rather than a research contribution appropriate for the ICML main track. It introduces no new algorithms, theoretical results, or scientific discoveries.

Complete absence of empirical evaluation: There are no benchmarks, scalability studies, wall-clock timing comparisons, or convergence analyses demonstrating the claimed computational efficiency or correctness against standard suites (such as COCO or Nevergrad) or existing packages (such as DEAP or Pagmo).

Incomplete manuscript with missing text and links: Multiple sentences and sections contain glaring placeholders and omitted content, including missing repository and documentation links in the abstract and Section 4, a missing footnote URL on page 3, and a blank reference/text gap in Section 5 ('We have used it in our previous papers e.g., and expect it to...').

Unsubstantiated claims: Statements regarding significant speedups, modular maintenance, and reproducibility reports are asserted without presenting supporting data, protocols, or experimental results in the text.

strengths: PyPop7 brings together an extensive collection of population-based black-box optimization algorithms (>72 variants across 13 families), with special emphasis on high-dimensional methods.
The library adopts a clean, NumPy-centric API that is easy to understand and integrate into Python workflows, as illustrated in the usage example.
The emphasis on reproducibility via explicit random seed control and code-based repeatability reports is commendable for scientific computing.
weaknesses: The paper is structured as an open-source software announcement (similar in format to a JMLR MLOSS paper) and does not present original research contributions, new algorithmic methodologies, or theoretical advancements required for the ICML main research track.

There are no empirical evaluations, runtime comparisons, or benchmark results presented against standard alternatives (such as Nevergrad, PaGMO, DEAP, or Optuna) to substantiate claims of computational efficiency and scalability.

The manuscript contains incomplete text and missing placeholders, including missing URLs in the abstract and footnotes ('available at and respectively') and missing citations in Section 5 ('in our previous papers e.g., and expect it to').
Technical details regarding the modular architecture, parallel execution backends, and memory optimizations are only mentioned in passing without substantive design or implementation analysis.

strengths: Wide algorithmic breadth: PyPop7 aims to support over 72 variants across 13 population-based black-box optimization (BBO) families, which represents a large software integration effort.
Specialized focus on high-dimensional and large-scale BBO techniques (e.g., limited-memory approximations, space decomposition, coordinate smoothing).
Clear and standardized API design demonstrated through a straightforward Python usage example integrated with NumPy.
weaknesses: Mismatch with research track expectations: The manuscript is written purely as an open-source software release announcement (similar to a JMLR MLOSS stub) rather than a research contribution. It presents no new algorithmic methodologies, theoretical analyses, or novel scientific insights.

Complete absence of empirical evaluation: There are no benchmark experiments, runtime comparisons, scaling profiles, or convergence evaluations comparing PyPop7 against established libraries (such as Nevergrad, EvoTorch, PyCMA, or DEAP). As a result, claims about computational efficiency and performance on high-dimensional problems remain unsupported.

Unfinished text and missing placeholders: The manuscript contains multiple unpopulated blanks and broken references, such as missing URLs in the abstract ('available at and respectively') and Section 4 ('online documentations:'), a missing footnote/link in Section 3, and a missing citation in Section 5 ('our previous papers e.g., and expect').

Inadequate paper length and depth: At only four pages of high-level overview, the paper lacks detailed discussions on implementation architecture, memory management, vectorization mechanisms, and handling of constraints or noise.
